records.label: Large Ohio kindred
records.onset: spasticity/weakness first year to sixth decade; dystonia first to third decade
quotes: We report clinical and genetic data from large Ohio kindred with autosomal dominant (AD) HSP and DYT.

Age of onset of spasticity and weakness is from the first year to the sixth decade, and age of onset of DYT from the first to third decade. There is no ataxia or apparent cognitive involvement. Neuroimaging and peripheral neurophysiology are normal.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial ATP synthase complex

records.segregation: Sanger sequencing showed only affected individuals carrying the variant; cosegregated with affected individuals
quotes: The autosomal dominant pedigree included 40 individuals, of which 18 were affected with either childhood-onset, progressive generalized dystonia or adult-onset, gradually progressive spastic paraplegia. Less severe, later-onset, focal limb and neck dystonia and spasmodic dysphonia also occurred, possibly related to trauma or overuse.
In brief, the proband had unilateral upper limb onset at age 2 years that generalized to trunk and all limbs, resulting in loss of ambulation.
Consistent with the pedigree phenotypes, Sanger sequencing showed only affected individuals carrying the ATP5MC3 variant.
records.genotype_reason: single heterozygous variant; mode as stated for the family

records.label: Family-2 proband
quotes: The proband of this family was a right-handed male, born to healthy unrelated parents of European descent with no family history of dystonia or related movement disorders, who first presented to the Department of pediatric neurology in Freiburg (Germany) at the age of 11 years with a 4-year history of gradually worsening upper limb dystonia.

Brain MRI revealed nonspecific mild frontoparietal white-matter changes bilaterally without other associated abnormalities. However, parent-offspring trio WES revealed a NM_001689.4:c.318C>G (p.Asn106Lys) variant as a heterozygous, de novo mutation in the proband

notes.statement: Zech et al. (2022) identified de novo heterozygous missense variants in ATP5MC3 (N106K, P107A, G79V) in 3 unrelated patients with dystonia and/or spasticity. All three variants affected strictly conserved residues in the C-terminal helical motifs of the protein and were absent from gnomAD.
quotes: De-novo monoallelic ATP5MC3 missense variants were prioritized in three individuals (patients 8-10) (Figure 5a and 5b).

All substitutions affected stringently conserved amino-acid residues located in close proximity within the carboxy-terminal helical motifs of the protein (Figure 5c); two variants occurred at directly neighboring nucleotides.

notes.statement: Zech et al. (2022) found that the ATP5MC3 G79V variant caused a significantly greater ATPase enzyme deficit than the N106K variant. G79V was associated with a more severe presentation of neurodevelopmental disease with spasticity, and N106K with isolated dystonia. The authors cautioned that further studies were needed before genotype-phenotype correlations could be clearly postulated.
quotes: our experiments performed for patients 8 and 10 revealed that ATP5MC3 c.236G>T, associated with a more severe neurodevelopmental disease-spasticity presentation, produced a significantly greater ATPase enzyme deficit than ATP5MC3 c.318C>G, associated with isolated dystonia. However, further studies are required before genotype-phenotype correlations can be clearly postulated.

notes.statement: Zech et al. (2022) combined their 3 ATP5MC3 patients with the multigenerational family reported by Neilson et al. Across these individuals, features included dystonia (12/18), spasticity/pyramidal signs (17/18) and developmental delay/intellectual disability (2/18).
quotes: features of the ATP5MC3-associated condition include dystonia (12/18), spasticity/pyramidal signs (17/18), and developmental delay/intellectual disability (2/18). Dystonia-predominant syndromes were documented in 10 individuals (patients 8 and 9; eight subjects from the multigenerational family).

notes.statement: Zech et al. (2022) suggested that dominant-negative effects could underlie disease caused by the ATP5MC3 and ATP5F1A variants. This was supported by mild-to-moderate ATPase assembly and/or enzyme-activity defects in patient cell lines. Structural modeling placed G79V at an interhelical contact site and the N106 and P107 residues at the site of FO-F1 subcomplex interaction.
quotes: Dominant-negative effects could well be possible, as supported by the observation of mild-to-moderate ATPase assembly and/or enzyme-activity defects in several patient lines.

we observed that p.Gly79Val was positioned at an interhelical contact side, while the other modeled variants were situated in immediate vicinity of a loop structure essentially involved in the interaction between the FO and F1 subcomplexes (Figure 5d).

notes.statement: Zech et al. (2022) estimated that phenotypes related to mutations in nuclear ATPase-encoding genes accounted for 0.3% (5/1,950) of patients with suspected mitochondrial disease and 0.2% (2/1,012) of patients with dystonia.
quotes: we estimate the frequencies of phenotypes related to mutations in nuclear ATPase-encoding genes at 0.3% (5/1,950) and 0.2% (2/1,012), respectively

notes.statement: Neilson et al. (2022) found that complex I through IV activities were normal in fibroblasts from the Family-1 proband (dystonia) and his affected father (HSP), but complex V activity was reduced by 20%, with a 20 to 32% reduction in cellular ATP and a 21 to 25% reduction in oxygen consumption. Because oxygen consumption and ATP fell in proportion, the results did not support uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation as the mechanism.
quotes: activities of electron transport chain complexes I through IV were equivalent to controls. However, Complex V activity was reduced by 20% (p < 0.01) (Figure 2). Similarly, cellular ATP was reduced 20% to 32% and oxygen consumption 21% to 25% (Figure 2).
Uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation, however, was not supported as a mechanism for the human mutation, as both oxygen consumption and ATP were proportionally reduced.

notes.statement: Neilson et al. (2022) expressed the Drosophila ATPsynC (CG1746) homolog carrying the human-equivalent p.N102K mutation or the E. coli-equivalent p.N102E mutation under the arm-GAL4 driver. Both mutant lines showed reduced mobility in geotaxis assays, with p.N102K the slowest. Complex V activity was reduced by 53% in p.N102K flies and by 37% in p.N102E flies.
quotes: At less than one week of age, the human disease mutant subunit c (p.N102K) and the equivalent bacterial mutation (p.N102E) demonstrated reduced mobility relative to wild type flies and the arm-GAL4; UAS-WT construct
the Complex V activity was reduced by 53% for the human p.N102K mutant (p=0.0008) and by 37% for the bacterial p.N102E mutant (p=0.003)

notes.statement: Neilson et al. (2022) screened 384 patients with dystonia (n = 362) or hereditary spastic paraplegia (n = 22) for variants in ATP5MC1, ATP5MC2, and ATP5MC3 and found no deleterious variants.
quotes: To identify additional subunit c variants in patients with dystonia or spastic paraplegia, 384 patients were screened for variants in ATP5MC1, ATP5MC2, and ATP5MC3. No deleterious variants were identified in the cohort of patients with dystonia or spastic paraplegia

notes.statement: Neilson et al. (2022) noted that 2 paralogs, ATP5MC1 and ATP5MC2, also encode subunit c, so haploinsufficiency of ATP5MC3 would be unlikely to explain the severe phenotypes. They hypothesized that the mutant protein interferes with the F1-F0 interaction at a conserved loop. They suggested that the relative expression of the mutant gene in different tissues may influence which phenotype develops.
quotes: Assuming equal expression of the three alleles, haploinsufficiency would be unlikely to account for the severe phenotypes, as 83% of the active protein would still remain. Thus, we hypothesized that the presence of the mutant allele interfered with the F1-F0 interaction which could be tested through overexpression.
Thus, we suspect that relative expression of the mutated gene may mediate phenotypic expression.

notes.statement: Neilson et al. (2022) stated that in Family-1, dystonia can generalize when it begins in childhood, shows incomplete penetrance, and responds to pallidal deep brain stimulation. The spastic paraplegia began in adulthood, progressed gradually, and was not accompanied by other neurologic problems.
quotes: Dystonia in this pedigree can generalize if manifest in childhood, shows incomplete penetrance, and responds to pallidal deep brain stimulation. The spastic paraplegia presents in adulthood, progresses gradually, and is not accompanied by other neurological problems.

notes.statement: Neilson et al. (2022) reported that bilateral pallidal deep brain stimulation, implanted at age 9 years, restored ambulation and limb use in the Family-1 proband with generalized dystonia, and the response remained excellent at age 25 years.
quotes: Bilateral pallidal deep brain stimulation, implanted at age 9 years, restored ambulation and limb use. At age 25 years, his response remains excellent.

notes.statement: Neilson et al. (2022) noted that linkage analysis in the large family had previously mapped the disorder to chromosome 2q24-q31. Whole-exome sequencing restricted to this region identified the ATP5MC3 variant as the only shared novel coding variant.
quotes: In a large pedigree with an unusual phenotype of spastic paraplegia or dystonia and autosomal dominant inheritance, linkage analysis previously mapped the disease to chromosome 2q24-2q31.
restricted to novel shared coding variants within the linkage region, identified a single missense variant

notes.statement: Gilbert et al. (2009) used single and multipoint linkage analysis with microsatellite and SNP array genotyping in a large multigenerational Ohio kindred. They mapped the disease locus to chromosome 2q24-q31, flanked by markers rs1424937 and rs1559510. This region lies proximal to SPG13 and contains no known HSP or dystonia genes.
quotes: The disease locus was mapped to a region on chromosome 2q 24-31, flanked by markers rs1424937-rs1559510, proximal to SPG13, in a region where there are no known HSP or DYT genes.

notes.statement: In a secondary analysis looking for candidate genes that segregated with the dystonia phenotype, Gilbert et al. (2009) found two candidate regions with parametric lod scores above 2.0.
quotes: A secondary analysis for candidate genes segregating with the DYT phenotype revealed two candidate regions with parametric lod scores above 2.0.

notes.statement: Gilbert et al. (2009) reported that deep brain stimulation markedly improved generalized dystonia in 1 affected child.
quotes: Generalized DYT improved markedly with deep brain stimulation in 1 child.

notes.statement: Gilbert et al. (2009) described the disorder in the Ohio kindred as autosomal dominant and highly penetrant.
quotes: a large, multigenerational family with a novel, AD, highly penetrant neurological disease causing spasticity and DYT
